headline_marked: [[NASA seeks private sector help]] to save Hubble Space Telescope from crashing by 2030s
headline: NASA seeks private sector help to save Hubble Space Telescope from crashing by 2030s
summary: The iconic Hubble Space Telescope is slowly falling and will re-enter Earth's atmosphere in the early to mid-2030s unless its orbit is boosted. NASA is inviting commercial proposals to extend its operational life.
details: The Hubble Space Telescope is facing an inevitable re-entry into Earth's atmosphere in the early to mid-2030s if its orbit isn't boosted. Gravity is slowly pulling the famed telescope closer, threatening its operational life. NASA has now opened a Request for Information (RFI) to the private sector, seeking innovative solutions to save it.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman emphasized the telescope's ongoing scientific value, stating, "Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible." Extending its life promises more discoveries and a deeper understanding of the universe.

The agency is committed to exploring cost-effective ways to maintain this valuable asset, owing it to taxpayers and the scientific community. Interested commercial entities have until November 30th at 3 PM ET to submit their proposals.

topic: jackery launches smaller portable power station
headline_marked: [[Jackery launches its smallest power station yet]], the Explorer 100D, weighing just 1.87 lbs
headline: Jackery launches its smallest power station yet, the Explorer 100D, weighing just 1.87 lbs
summary: The new Explorer 100D features a durable lithium iron phosphate battery and is available for $99, offering 96Wh capacity in a compact design.
details: Jackery has unveiled its smallest portable power station to date, the Explorer 100D. Measuring just 4.6 x 3.4 x 3.4 inches and weighing 1.87 pounds, it features a long-lasting lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery.

With a 96Wh (30,000mAh) capacity, the Explorer 100D is designed for up to 8 years of regular use, boasting a 3,000 charge cycle lifespan. This LFP technology offers significantly greater longevity than competing products with standard lithium-ion cells.
The Explorer 100D will be available starting November 15th at Walmart for $99. It is already available at Costco in a two-pack for $179.99.

The device includes two 140W USB-C ports and one 18W USB-A port, with a total maximum output of 158W. It also supports up to 100W of direct solar input, allowing it to charge to 80% capacity in about 1.5 hours.
